_doc: Commitments for /hyderabad/commitments. Edit rows under payload.commitments and set payload.updated, then run: python3 neer-vazhvu-api/scripts/build_commitments.py --city hyderabad. The status rule and the checks are in that script's docstring.

provenance.note: Curated commitment register - per-entry dated citations carry the accountability. Six of seven entries are marked unverified because the promise was announced without a dated deliverable, which is the finding rather than a gap in the data.

payload.headline: What Hyderabad has been promised about its water
payload.intro: Dated, public undertakings about Hyderabad's water, each with the citation that records it. A status only changes here when a dated citation supports the change - not when a deadline passes quietly, and not on the basis of a press release restating an old target as a new one. Where a promise involves a number we have been unable to source from the promising authority, that is said in the entry rather than smoothed over.

status_legend.on-track: Evidence of progress against the stated date, from a dated source
status_legend.overdue: The stated date has passed without a dated source recording completion
status_legend.unverified: We can cite the promise but cannot yet cite its current status either way.

commitments.title: Musi Riverfront Development, Phase I
commitments.committed_by: Government of Telangana / Musi Riverfront Development Corporation
commitments.what: Rejuvenation of a 55 km stretch of the Musi from Gandipet to Gowrelly, championed by Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy. In May 2026 the state released Rs 375 crore as the first instalment against Rs 1,500 crore earmarked in the 2026-27 budget. On 2 July 2026 the state Cabinet accorded administrative approval for Phase I at an estimated cost of Rs 7,345.12 crore (Deccan Chronicle, 3 July 2026), and on 9 July 2026 the Chief Secretary inspected Phase I progress.

commitment_source.label: Siasat, reporting the Metropolitan Area and Urban Development Department's order of 6 May 2026 releasing Rs 375 crore as the first instalment for the Musi rejuvenation project, against Rs 1,500 crore allocated for 2026-27

status_history.note: Funds released and progress inspected, but no published completion date for Phase I and no public milestone schedule to measure against. Recorded as unverified rather than on-track: money moving is not the same as a deadline being met.
status_history.source_label: Devdiscourse (ANI), reporting the Telangana government's statement on the Chief Secretary's inspection of the Musi Riverfront Phase-I stretch, 9 July 2026 (no completion date or milestone schedule given)

status_history.note: MRDCL invited bids on 12 Oct 2026 for the two Phase I works: Zone-IA, Himayat Sagar to Bapughat (Ch. 1+320 m to Ch. 8+850 m), and Zone-IB, Osman Sagar to Bapughat (Ch. 0+690 m to Ch. 12+212 m), each 'under EPC Turnkey Basis/ Design Build Contract including O&M for 05 years'. Bids are due '26-11-2026 up to 5:00 PM' and technical bids open '27-11-2026 onwards 11:00 AM'. Deccan Chronicle reported on 3 July 2026, after the Cabinet approved Phase I at Rs 7,345.12 crore, a plan to 'award contracts by August 19'; we have not found a record of an award. A contract award is a stage rather than a progress figure, and the notice gives no completion date, so the status stays unverified.
status_history.source_label: MRDCL Invitation for Bids, Tender Notices No. 06/CE/MRDCL/2026-27 and 07/CE/MRDCL/2026-27, Dt. 12-10-2026 (Phase I, Zones IA and IB), linked from MRDCL's Tenders page

commitments.note: The riverfront programme is the single largest thing being done to the Musi and the hardest to hold to account, because no dated deliverable has been published. A phase-wise milestone schedule is the document to ask for.

commitments.title: Intercept and treat all sewage entering the Musi along the 34 km Bapu Ghat to Gowrelly stretch
commitments.what: Interception and diversion of sewage outfalls before they reach the river, along a 34 km reach, as the sewage-side counterpart to the riverfront works. This is the load-bearing claim in every Musi cleanup plan: without interception, riverfront construction changes the banks and not the water.

commitment_source.label: The Hans India - Musi makeover: sewage interception and decentralised treatment

status_history.note: No public reporting of how many outfalls along the 34 km reach have actually been intercepted. The count of trapped-versus-remaining outfalls is the verification instrument, and it is not published.
status_history.source_label: The Hans India, reporting officials on the Musi Riverfront Development Corporation's interception plan for the 34 km Bapu Ghat to Gowrelly stretch, 21 April 2026 (gives no count of intercepted outfalls)

commitments.note: Delhi's equivalent commitment - trapping 39 drains to the Yamuna - is trackable because the trapped count is reported. Hyderabad's is not.

commitments.title: 39 new sewage treatment plants along the Musi under AMRUT
commitments.committed_by: HMWSSB, under the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation
commitments.what: 39 STPs totalling a reported 972 MLD, described as progressing under AMRUT, on top of an existing estate and a further tranche said to be already commissioned.

commitment_source.label: Construction World - Hyderabad's Musi river revitalised (STP programme figures)

status_history.note: The Government of Telangana's action-taken report to the NGT in OA 606/2018 (figures as on 31.12.2024) gives 'Existing STPs Capacity (25 Nos)' as 772.30 MLD and 'Newly Constructed & commissioned STPs (11 Nos)' as 663.00 MLD, says '36 STPs of capacity 1435.30 MLD are in operation', and says that once 9 STPs of 443 MLD under construction are completed 'the total capacity of STPs in GHMC area would be 1878 MLD' (PDF pp21-22). HMWSSB, in a press release reported by Siasat on 4 Sep 2025, gives '39 STPs with a capacity of 972 million litres per day (MLD)' sanctioned under AMRUT 2.0 at Rs 3,849.10 crore. These count different sets of plants (existing, newly built in GHMC, and sanctioned under AMRUT 2.0), so each is quoted as its source prints it and they are not added together. HMWSSB's RTI 4(1)(b) disclosure or an annual report would set out the whole estate in one place.
status_history.source_label: Government of Telangana, action-taken report to the NGT in OA 606/2018 (in compliance of the order dated 22.08.2024; figures as on 31.12.2024), PDF pp21-22

commitments.note: Official figures exist for the GHMC estate: the Government of Telangana's NGT filing gives '36 STPs of capacity 1435.30 MLD' in operation as on 31.12.2024. They count different plants from the 39 sanctioned under AMRUT 2.0, so the two are quoted separately and not added into one treatment-capacity number.

commitments.title: HYDRAA to restore 10 lakes a year, toward 200 rejuvenated lakes
commitments.committed_by: Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA)
commitments.what: A stated target of ten lake restorations a year against a vision of 200 restored lakes. Six lakes were taken up in a first phase and 14 more are to be restored in a second, and restoration of four more began on 25 June 2026 with bhoomi puja at Ibrahim Pedda Cheruvu (Rajendranagar), Bhagirathamma Cheruvu (Gandipet), Kamuni Cheruvu (Moosapet) and Kapra Cheruvu (Medchal-Malkajgiri).

commitment_source.label: The Week - HYDRAA reshapes Hyderabad through lake restoration and land protection

status_history.note: The Week reports that HYDRAA 'is currently reviving six lakes, three of which were inaugurated by the chief minister in March', that 'Another 20 are in the pipeline', and a 'target of restoring 10 lakes a year'.
status_history.source_label: The Week, on HYDRAA's lake restoration, 25 April 2026 (online 26 April 2026)

status_history.note: Siasat reports that HYDRAA 'had undertaken the development of six lakes as phase one and will restore 14 more as part of phase two', and that the HYDRAA Commissioner began restoration of four more lakes on 25 June 2026 (Ibrahim Pedda Cheruvu, Bhagirathamma Cheruvu, Kamuni Cheruvu and Kapra Cheruvu) at a combined Rs 107 crore. Neither this report nor The Week's of April 2026 gives a count of lakes completed each year to set against the stated ten a year, so the status is unverified rather than on-track.
status_history.source_label: Siasat, reporting the HYDRAA Commissioner's bhoomi puja for four lakes, 25 June 2026

commitments.note: The Week reports a target of restoring 10 lakes a year and a vision of '200 rejuvenated lakes across Hyderabad within a decade'. The metropolitan register holds 2,978 lakes.

commitments.title: Complete the gazetted Full Tank Level notifications for the region's lakes
commitments.what: Every lake is meant to receive a preliminary FTL notification and then a final one after objections. All 2,978 lakes in the register have the preliminary; 1,352 have the final, leaving 1,626 without a legally settled boundary.

commitment_source.label: HMDA gazetted lake register (the register is itself the record of progress)

status_history.note: Final notifications ran at 152 in 2016 then effectively stopped - 10, 60, 2, 3 and 2 across 2017-2023. Then 533 in 2024, 533 in 2025 and 57 so far in 2026: two-thirds of every final notification ever issued arrived in the last two years. Directly measurable from the register, which is why this entry can carry a status the others cannot.
status_history.source_label: HMDA gazetted lake register, lakes.hmda.gov.in (preliminary and final FTL notification dates for each lake), counted 26 Jul 2026

commitments.note: The one Hyderabad commitment we can audit continuously, because the promising authority publishes the register that records it. Rangareddy remains the laggard at 34.5% finally notified against 68.0% in Siddipet.

commitments.title: Hold elections to the three new municipal corporations
commitments.committed_by: Telangana State Election Commission / Government of Telangana
commitments.what: Elections to seven municipal corporations and 116 municipalities were held on 11 February 2026, but the three Hyderabad corporations - GHMC, Cyberabad and Malkajgiri - were deferred to a later date following the trifurcation. Until they are held the corporations are administered by a Special Officer and there are no elected councillors.

commitment_source.label: Telangana municipal elections held 11 February 2026; GHMC and two other corporations deferred

status_history.note: No polling date announced for the three Hyderabad corporations as of this compilation. Recorded because it is the reason the ward-representative surface on this site is empty rather than incomplete.
status_history.source_label: Telangana State Election Commission website, notifications (the latest under Urban Local Bodies > GHMC is dated 04/02/2025, and none sets a poll for GHMC, Cyberabad or Malkajgiri), viewed 18 Oct 2026

commitments.note: Directly relevant to water accountability: 300 wards were gazetted in December 2025 and nobody has yet been elected to any of them.

commitments.title: Publish the encroachment count GHMC's own drain layer defines
commitments.committed_by: GHMC (implicit - the schema is published, the data is not)
commitments.what: GHMC's storm-water drain layer defines fields for encroachments per nala, separated into government, private and religious, with a count of cases in court. All five fields are published as zero for all 96 nalas.

commitment_source.label: GHMC nala layer via OpenCity - fields present and uniformly empty, verified 2026-07-26

status_history.note: Not a promise the city made in words, but a disclosure it designed and did not complete. Included because the schema specifies exactly what to request, which makes it the most actionable information gap on this page.
status_history.source_label: GHMC 'Hyderabad Nalas' layer on OpenCity, last modified 25 Nov 2025 (Govt_Encr, Pvt_Encr, Rel_Encr, Total_Encr and Court_Case read 0 for all 96 nalas)

commitments.note: In a city that created an agency to demolish encroachments, a column of zeros is an unfilled field rather than a clean record. Tracked here so the day it is populated is visible.

payload.update_model: Status changes require a dated citation. A deadline passing does not by itself move an entry to 'overdue' unless a due date was publicly stated - most Hyderabad water commitments are announced without one, which is why 'unverified' is the most common status on this page rather than a hedge.
payload.sources_note: Several entries rest on news reporting because the underlying government orders and programme schedules are not published. Where a figure is contested across sources - above all the STP counts - the entry says so instead of picking one. Provenance discipline for the whole city is documented in docs/cities/hyderabad/data-sources.md.
